title: China's Buick Electra GS Is A Stylish Hybrid America Can't Have - CarScoops
content: GM could definitely use plug-in hybrid sedan in its U.S. lineup Buick hasn't offered a sedan in the U.S. since sales of the Regal ended in 2020. But it's a totally different story in China, where SUV haters can choose from multiple low-riding four-door cars, including the handsome, electrified Electra L7. Now, Buick's Chinese division is gearing up to launch its Electra GS little brother, and you have to wonder if America is missing out. Details of the Electra GS were revealed by China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology filings ahead of the official debut, and they tell us the production car has changed quite a bit since GM showed the Electra GS concept (below) at the Shanghai Auto Show in 2025. The LED headlights have been inverted, and the Buick badge moved from the hood to a front facia that features less body-color plastic. The concept was incredibly handsome, but maybe looked a little too much like a Tesla Model 3 around the front. The production car looks less like a Tesla, but sacrifices some eye candy points. An imminent ban on pop-out door handles in China meant the concept's had to go, and though the fastback profile is carried across, the show car's traditional sedan trunk has made way for a more practical hatch. The taillights are also new, and so is the "Buick" lettering spelled out at the rear of the car. Another genuinely massive change is the productions GS's massive reduction in scale. MIIT data shows it's 196.1 inches (4,980 mm) long, but the concept (pictured above) was a huge 208.7 inches (5,300 mm). Same thing with wheelbase. The concept's axles were 126 inches (3,200 mm) apart, but the production GS wheelbase measures 112.8 inches (2,865 mm), making the finished car similar in size to a Toyota Crown, rather than a Mercedes S-Class. The biggest switch of all, though, takes place under the hood. GM didn't reveal much in the way of technical details about the concept, but it did confirm it was a fully electric car that rode on a dedicated EV platform, giving a totally flat floor. But, like Adam West's 1966 Batman jumping on the Batpoles inside Wayne Manor dressed in a comfy cardigan, and emerging inside the Batcave in full caped crusader garb 100 ft (31 m) down, the GS bound for dealers has arrived for duty as a plug-in hybrid. Base cars pair a 97 horsepower (98 PS) naturally aspirated 1.5-liter inline-4 with a 221 hp (224 PS) electric motor, but a more expensive variant swaps the NA gas motor for a turbocharged version of the same, making 154 hp (156 PS). We'll have wait for the full China debut to find out more about the GS, including whether the interior looks anything like the concept's (below). But don't pin your hopes on seeing that yoke steering wheel — we can already see a conventional steering wheel is present in the studio images of the exterior. Back in the U.S., GM's sales have been hurt by its lack of hybrid offerings. The automaker was so sure EVs would dominate the car market by the end of the decade that it didn't bother developing them, except for the Corvette E-Ray (now renamed Grand Sport X). Rival brands like Toyota and Hyundai hedged their bets, and made both, and are now reaping the rewards, while GM is rushing to catch up toward the end of the decade. Could the GS work here? Absolutely, but it's not likely. GM does import vehicles from China, including Chinese-built Buick Envision from China, although production of that model is due to shift to Kansas in 2028. Complicating matters is the fact that the GS is the result of a joint venture between GM and China's SAIC, and new restrictions on Chinese software that take effect with the 2027 model year would make it tricky to get this car compliant for the U.S. market, even if production was shifted to North America to avoid tariffs. Overall, we'd say don't hold your breath for this Buick.

title: Crazy Like Jeremy Fox: Birdie G’s Returns While The Restaurant at Edna Marks a New Chapter - Observer
content: What is it like to open two high-profile restaurants, in two different cities, in less than two weeks? For chef Jeremy Fox, it’s a crazy but surprisingly calming experience. By clicking submit, you agree to our terms of service and acknowledge we may use your information to send you emails, product samples, and promotions on this website and other properties. You can opt out anytime. Fox, a versatile chef who followed up his “On Vegetables” cookbook with his “On Meat” cookbook, has worked in the top tier of fine dining in California and also created comforting, nostalgic food that celebrates Americana and the Jewish-American diaspora. In Los Angeles, he’s long been a leader of seasonal, market-driven cuisine. But recently, it was unclear whether he would cook in a restaurant again. He closed Birdie G’s, a deeply personal restaurant named for his daughter and inspired by his grandmother’s home cooking, in Santa Monica at the end of 2025. The closure, one of many in L.A. spurred by an economic downturn, left Fox unmoored. But now Birdie G’s is back, with an expanded repertoire, at a high-profile new location in Los Angeles. On October 26, Fox opened the new Birdie G’s inside the Fairmont Century Plaza hotel. Unlike the previous dinner-only Birdie G’s, the new restaurant serves breakfast, lunch and dinner. “It’s a muscle I’ve never used before,” Fox told Observer on opening night after we ate his fried-oyster-topped riff on Caesar salad, soul-warming matzo ball soup, “pickle chick” schnitzel and Flannery steak frites before indulging in a slice of jiggly rose petal pie. What added to the craziness is that Fox knew he would be in San Luis Obispo a few days later for friends-and-family service at The Restaurant at Edna. Fox and former Birdie G’s executive chef Matthew Schaler will open that vineyard restaurant, with a focus on local agriculture, on Thursday, November 5. The timing of restaurant openings is always unpredictable, and the original goal was to open Birdie G’s and The Restaurant at Edna months apart. “I will say that I planned to open both restaurants in the same week,” Fox joked this week when Observer asked him about his intense timeline. “That was the goal. I nailed it.” But the reality is, he is now the opposite of unmoored, and it’s a good feeling. “I’ve made no attempts to hide that I deal with anxiety,” Fox, who’s known for speaking freely about his mental health, tells Observer. “I spent much of this year pretty deep in anxiety because I didn’t have a place to go every day. I was used to having deadlines every day. I had to be ready for service every day. And my deadlines were all, like, eight months away. It was an anxiety of, like, ‘Am I achieving as much in my day as I should?’ … But as things ramped up in the last two-and-a-half months, I’ve actually been calmer. I’ve always been someone who, the more engaged I am, the more semi-overwhelmed I am, the calmer I am, and the more I’m able to block out the noise. As it’s gotten crazier, I’ve gotten calmer.” It helps, of course, that he’s got an arsenal of dishes and techniques that he’s honed for decades. At Birdie G’s, he’s put a Rancho Gordo yellow eye bean stew on the lunch menu. That stew originated at Manresa, when David Kinch asked Fox to help create a patio menu. Fox then served the stew at Ubuntu and Rustic Canyon. The stew “appears to have an ungodly amount of garlic,” Fox says. “The garlic has to be cooked a certain amount, or else it disappears or overpowers the stew. It’s a matter of toasting the rosemary, the chili flakes and the garlic and olive oil, but not to the point where the garlic takes on any color. But it does have to be cooked through.” Meanwhile, making Birdie G’s matzo ball soup, which is enriched with carrot miso, is a “regimented” process. Fox was influenced by both how his grandmother Gladys made matzo ball soup and how specific his wife, Rachael Sheridan, is about chicken broth when she makes matzo ball soup. Birdie G’s is about Fox’s family and his desire to make everyday food. The Restaurant at Edna, with its focus on seasonal cooking and regional wines, is about using a different kind of muscle, one that Fox has called upon a lot in his career. “It’s designed for the things I’m good at,” Fox says of the dinner-only, five-night-a-week restaurant. “There’s no concept to it. This is one of the ways I like to cook, where the menu changes constantly. It’s based on the buildability of the best local ingredients, prepared thoughtfully. Not fussy, though. The room begs itself to be a destination restaurant, but we really want to try to not fall into that. We want to be someplace where you can go every week, and there will be new things on the menu as well as things you remember that you had last time. And then dishes might be gone forever, or they might come back next year.” During friends-and-family dinners, Fox and Schaler got raves for dishes like cone cabbage stuffed with smoked bacon, ramps and an egg-yolk sauce; sweet potato and pumpkin pavé with brown butter sabayon, sage and truffles; and mushroom ravioli shaped like mushrooms and featuring fonduta made with Stepladder Moonstone cheese. There’s also the Edna salad, with a beet-based French dressing that Schaler impressed Fox with when he was applying to work at the original Birdie G’s. The Restaurant at Edna will serve local seafood like Petrale sole and California meat like Flannery beef. Fox is buying ingredients from nearby farms that previously supplied him in Los Angeles for more than a decade. He’s looking at shellfish from uni diver Stephanie Mutz. This is his wheelhouse. But life, as Fox has long known, is about different things being true at the same time. Fox and his family eat at Silver Lake’s Astro diner more than any other restaurant in Los Angeles. He very much wants Birdie G’s to be a comforting, unintimidating, everyday L.A. restaurant. “The restaurants that originally inspired me to want to be part of the restaurant business were Applebee’s, Chili’s, The Cheesecake Factory, those kinds of places,” Fox says. “I went to culinary school and followed the path of fine dining when, originally, all I wanted to do was have a place that people like to go eat.” “It’s accessible food,” he says. “It’s recognizable. The original Birdie G’s was a crowd-pleaser. People who came really loved it and connected with it. A lot of people would say they haven’t had anything like that since their grandmother cooked it.” But most grandmothers don’t do things like make a Caesar salad enhanced by “A.C.G.” powder with anchovies, capers and garlic that are cooked down in olive oil for more than a day and then strained and dehydrated. Fox thinks a lot about the two dramatically contrasting restaurants in the movie “Big Night” and how he finds them both compelling. “Birdie G’s, for me, was a way to kind of have one foot in both worlds, with the understated subtle cuisine and also the more over-the-top and accessible food while trying to be a little bit subversive,” he says. The food at Birdie G’s is delicious and fun and a little crazy. For Fox, there’s comfort in the craziness. We get it: you like to have control of your own internet experience. title: Text of Pope Leo's Nov. 4 general audience - Catholic Standard
content: The following is the full text of Pope Leo XIV’s general audience address given Nov. 4 at St. Peter’s Square. The Documents of the Second Vatican Council. IV. Constitution Gaudium et Spes. 8. Faith and social, political, and economic life Dear brothers and sisters, good morning and welcome! The social dimension is an integral part not only of human nature, but also of our faith in Christ Jesus, as the precious legacy we receive from the Incarnation of the Son of God. The Constitution Gaudium et Spes (GS) recalls this in Chapters III and IV of Part II, dedicated to economic and social life and to the life of the political community. In these areas too, the Christian faith offers criteria for discernment. The Council Fathers highlight, first of all, the threat to world peace deriving from the imbalances linked to an economic development that is neither equitable nor respectful of creation (cf. GS, 63). This is a far-sighted vision, which was unfortunately borne out towards the end of the last century and which we see even more clearly today. To correct this course, the Document warns, technical progress alone is not enough: “many reforms in the socioeconomic realm and a change of mentality and attitude are required of all” (ibid.). Therefore, Gaudium et Spes summarizes the Christian vision of economic development, which must always be at the service of humankind and under human control (cf. GS, 64–65). The concept of integral development is already clearly evident here, a concept which Saint Paul VI would later place at the heart of his Encyclical Populorum Progressio (1967). More relevant than ever are the appeals to commit to eliminating discrimination against the most vulnerable social groups and migrants (cf. GS, 66). The heart of the economy is work. Through it, one develops as a person, provides for family needs, expresses one’s own talent, participates in social life and builds a better world by collaborating in God’s creative work. Work must never be distorted to the detriment of people, the common good or creation. The real challenge is to offer everyone opportunities to make the most of their abilities: unemployment, exploitation and working conditions that endanger health and life itself are unacceptable (cf. GS, 67). Workers have the right and the duty to participate in decisions affecting their work, including through trade unions, resolving conflicts through dialogue and non-violent action (cf. GS, 68). In this context, the Council recalls one of the fundamental principles of social teaching, namely the universal destination of earthly goods (cf. GS, 69) and applies it to the financial sphere, stating that “whoever makes decisions concerning these investments and the planning of the economy – whether they be individuals or groups of public authorities – are bound … to recognize their serious obligation of watching, on the one hand, that provision be made for the necessities required for a decent life both of individuals and of the whole community and, on the other, of looking out for the future and of establishing a right balance between the needs of present-day consumption, both individual and collective, and the demands of investing for the generation to come” (GS, 70). Gaudium et Spes then goes on to discuss the political community, noting several positive developments in the contemporary era, above all the fact that “the present keener sense of human dignity has given rise in many parts of the world to attempts to bring about a politico-juridical order which will give better protection to the rights of the person in public life” (GS, 73). The political community exists for the sake of the common good, which consists of “the sum of those conditions of the social life whereby men, families and associations more adequately and readily may attain their own perfection” (GS, 74). The exercise of political authority must always be directed towards the common good, which must be structured and operate according to local and historical circumstances, but always with the good of the entire human family at heart (cf. ibid.). Gaudium et Spes reiterates that “the Church and the political community in their own fields are autonomous and independent from each other. Yet both, under different titles, are devoted to the personal and social vocation of the same men. The more that both foster sounder cooperation between themselves with due consideration for the circumstances of time and place, the more effective will their service be exercised for the good of all” (GS, 76). Dear friends, engaging in economic and political life in accordance with these criteria is a way of building peace. As Pope Francis recalled, “war is a failure of politics and of humanity, a shameful capitulation, a stinging defeat before the forces of evil” (Encyclical Letter Fratelli tutti, 261). On the contrary, politics that tends to the wounds of peoples and of those who suffer injustice offers grounds for hope for the future of humanity. For this reason, I encourage young people to follow the example of those men and women who have borne faithful witness in these fields. And I renew my call to Christian communities to revive formation in the social doctrine of the Church. I greet all the English-speaking pilgrims and visitors taking part in today’s Audience, especially those from England, Ireland, Denmark, Malta, the Netherlands, Norway, Nigeria, Australia, Indonesia, Japan, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam and the United States of America. In a particular way, I welcome the members of the National Conference of Vocation Directors for England and Wales. Upon all of you and your families, I invoke the joy and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ. God bless you! Pope Leo XIV smiles from the popemobile while riding around St. Peter’s Square at the Vatican before his weekly general audience Nov. 4, 2026. (CNS photo/Lola Gomez)

title: General Motors taps PHEV sedan segment with Buick Electra GS - CarNewsChina.com
content: General Motors is ready to launch the Buick Electra GS plug-in hybrid sedan in China. Built jointly with SAIC, it will compete with some high-volume models from BYD and Geely. The Electra GS is on time, as Buick’s deliveries declined by 20.4% Year-Over-Year in China, according to China EV DataTracker. The Buick Electra GS was exposed in China by the local Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) during the domestic homologation process. It is a large sedan with dimensions of 4979/1914/1495 mm and a wheelbase of 2,865 mm. For clarity, it is 149 mm longer than the BYD Qin L DM-i sedan, marketed in some overseas markets under the Seal 6 name. The car’s exterior styling adopts a closed front end with a sizeable trapeze-shaped air intake, U-shaped headlights, semi-hidden door handles, a sleek roofline, a single taillight unit, and a ducktail spoiler. This sedan has approach and departure angles of 13 and 14 degrees, respectively. It rides on 18- or 19-inch wheels (225/50 R18 or 234/45 R19). The Electra GS can be optionally equipped with a roof-mounted LiDAR sensor. The curb weight lies between 1,780 and 1,890 kg. Its gross weight reaches 2,300 kg. The entry-level Buick Electra GS sedan comes standard with a 1.5-liter naturally aspirated 15FMC petrol-powered engine with a peak power output of 72 kW (97 hp). This ICE is manufactured by SAIC. The same ICE is used by the Roewe Jiayue 07 crossover, the Saic H5 (Shangjie H5), the Buick Electra E7 SUV, and other models. This engine is paired with a 165 kW (221 hp) electric motor. The car’s top speed is 190 km/h. It adopts two LFP battery pack variants from Zenergy and Rept Battero. A more powerful variant of the Buick Electra GS has a 1.5-liter turbocharged LD3 engine with a peak power output of 115 kW (154 hp). The same engine is used by the Buick Electra L7 sedan, the Buick GL8 PHEV minivan, and other cars. This ICE also works in pairs with a 165 kW (221 hp) electric motor. The top-trim Electra GS has a top speed of 190 km/h and a Zenergy-made LFP battery. It seems that the entry-level Buick Electra GS sedan will rival the mentioned BYD Qin L DM-i sedan. The latter model offers a combination of a 1.5-liter engine for 74 kW (99 hp) and an electric motor with a peak power output of 160 kW (215 hp). BYD delivered 70,740 units of this sedan to customers in China from January to September 2026, according to China EV DataTracker. The Electra GS is expected to cost more than 100,000 yuan (14,970 USD) domestically.

title: Buick Electra GS appears in China regulatory filing, expanding NEV lineup - CnEVPost
content: Buick's Electra GS plug-in hybrid sedan has appeared in China's latest regulatory filing catalog, revealing the fastback model's exterior and key powertrain specifications. China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology released its 413th batch of new vehicle filings on Tuesday, with public comments open from November 4 to 10. The Electra GS has 3 variants in the filings, all manufactured by SAIC-GM, covering 2 engine options and different battery cell suppliers. Buick is a brand under General Motors (NYSE: GM). All 3 variants feature an electric motor with a peak output of 165 kW (221 hp). Their engines each have a displacement of 1,498 milliliters, with rated outputs of 72 kW for 2 variants and 115 kW for the remaining variant. All 3 variants use lithium iron phosphate batteries. One uses cells supplied by Rept Battero Energy (HKEX: 666), while the other 2 use cells from Zenergy. Battery packs for all variants are produced by a SAIC-GM subsidiary. The filings do not list battery capacity or electric range. Filing images show the Electra GS with a coupe-like fastback profile, slim headlights, a full-width taillight and semi-hidden door handles, along with Electra GS badging at the rear. The 5-seat sedan measures 4,979 mm in length and 1,914 mm in width, with a wheelbase of 2,865 mm. Height varies slightly across the filed variants. The images show roof-mounted LiDAR, while the filings also list an option without LiDAR, alongside choices of rear spoilers, brake calipers and exterior trim. The filings do not disclose the supplier or specific capabilities of the driver-assistance system, nor do they detail final trim levels, pricing or launch timing. The Electra GS filing comes as Buick continues to update its new energy vehicle (NEV) lineup in China. On September 23, the brand launched an updated Electra E7 plug-in hybrid SUV, just 5 months after its initial launch. The Electra E7 update focused on powertrain and driver-assistance equipment, with the Pro trim combining a 1.5-liter turbocharged engine and advanced driver-assistance features. title: Former CEO of SGX-listed GS Holdings charged over false trading - The Business Times
content: Now known as Octopus (Apac) Holdings, the company has expanded into beverage distribution [SINGAPORE] The former CEO of GS Holdings, Pang Pok, was charged in court on Wednesday (Nov 4) with abetting a conspiracy to engage in share price manipulation and perverting the course of justice, said the Singapore Police Force. Pang, 68, who stepped down as CEO in 2024, is accused of conspiring with Koh Kim Seng, 62, and Chong Fatt, 60, to create a misleading appearance with respect to the price of GS Holdings’ securities between January 2022 and October 2023. The court documents did not state what roles Koh and Chong held in the company. Pang and Chong are also accused of deleting chat messages from their mobile phones relating to the alleged conspiracy. They face an additional charge of perverting the course of justice. All three men face, among other charges, one count each under the Securities and Futures Act. GS Holdings – behind several foodcourts and food centres in Singapore – was renamed  Octopus (Apac) Holdings  : 43A 0% in February 2026 and is listed on the Catalist board of the Singapore Exchange. Find out how enterprises are navigating power constraints and sustainability targets The Singapore-based company is now involved in beverage distribution. The charges arose from a joint investigation by the Commercial Affairs Department of the Singapore Police Force and the Monetary Authority of Singapore, following a referral from Singapore Exchange Regulation. If convicted, the accused face imprisonment of up to seven years, a fine of up to S$250,000, or both, for each charge relating to false trading. The penalty for perverting the course of justice includes imprisonment of up to seven years, a fine, or both. The charges come amid a series of corporate developments at Octopus (Apac) Holdings. The company appointed Paul Hopkins, formerly general manager of Maritime and Mercantile Asia Pacific, as its group CEO in October 2025. He stepped down from the role after less than a year, on Jul 21, 2026. The group’s expansion into beverage distribution began earlier in 2025. In May that year, it acquired Octopus Distribution Networks (ODN), which has since become the main focus of its F&B distribution business. ODN subsequently expanded its portfolio in September 2025 by agreeing to acquire the distribution business of LHA Food & Beverages for about S$3 million in cash. The transaction included the rights to distribute 11 Degree Premium Yanjing Beer in Singapore, as well as the trademarks of Rossl Bier and Como Bere. In February 2026, the company changed its name to Octopus (Apac) Holdings, to better reflect the business profile and strategic direction. The company entered into a conditional share sale-and-purchase agreement to dispose of its entire stake in wholly owned subsidiary Hawkerway to Wei Global for a net cash consideration of S$650,000. title: GS Retail Posts Record Quarterly Profit of 132.1 Billion Won - Seoul Economic Daily
content: GS Retail (007070.KS) said on the 4th that third-quarter revenue rose 3.4% from a year earlier to 3.31 trillion won ($2.3 billion), while operating profit climbed 18.9% to 132.1 billion won. Both figures marked record quarterly highs for the company. Earnings gains at its supermarket and home shopping units drove the improvement. SINGAPORE – The former chief executive of public-listed GS Holdings, a firm behind several foodcourts and food centres in Singapore, is facing a charge over allegations of share price manipulation. Pang Pok, 68, who stepped down as CEO in 2024, is said to have conspired with two others – Chong Fatt, 60, and Koh Kim Seng, 62 – to create a misleading appearance of the price of GS Holdings, whose shares were traded on the Catalist board of the Singapore Exchange. It was not stated in court documents what roles Chong and Koh had in GS Holdings. According to court documents, the three men allegedly pushed up the price of the firm’s securities by using three trading accounts to place orders and execute trades for GS Holdings’ securities between January 2022 and October 2023. Pang and Chong are also accused of perverting the course of justice by deleting text messages relating to the trades. All three men did not enter a plea on Nov 4. Their cases were adjourned to Dec 2 for them to engage lawyers. Pang’s bail amount was set at $120,000, while Chong’s was set at $40,000 and Koh’s at $30,000. According to SGX filings, GS Holdings changed its name earlier in 2026 to Octopus (APAC) Holdings to represent its ambition to become a leading food and beverage distribution partner in the Asia-Pacific region. Those convicted of committing false trading can be jailed for up to seven years, fined up to $250,000, or both. title: GS Retail Posts Record Profit Driven by Supermarkets, Home Shopping - 조선일보
content: Supermarkets, home shopping offset convenience store decline, driving GS Retail's highest-ever quarterly operating profit GS Retail, the distribution-focused affiliate of GS Group, recorded an operating profit of 132.1 billion Korean won in the third quarter of this year, marking its highest-ever performance for a single quarter. While the operating profit of its mainstay convenience store business declined, supermarkets and home shopping offset this by generating more than double the operating profit. GS Retail announced on the 4th that its third-quarter revenue reached 3.3143 trillion Korean won, a 3.4% increase from the same period last year. Operating profit rose 18.9% year-on-year to 132.1 billion Korean won. The revenue of GS25, its convenience store brand, amounted to 2.4743 trillion Korean won, up 1.1% year-on-year, setting a quarterly record. However, operating profit fell 8.1% to 78.2 billion Korean won. Compared to the second quarter of this year, when revenue and operating profit increased 7.1% and 21%, respectively, year-on-year, the growth in sales has slowed, and operating profit has turned to a decline. This is attributed to the high comparison base from last year’s third quarter, when convenience store sales surged due to consumer coupon effects. The overall performance was driven by supermarkets and home shopping. GS The Fresh, the supermarket division, reported third-quarter revenue of 527.7 billion Korean won and operating profit of 23.9 billion Korean won, up 14.9% and 159.8%, respectively. Both revenue and operating profit marked quarterly highs. The number of operating stores increased to 608, up 27 from a year ago, and existing store sales rose 10.7%. Delivery and pickup sales surged 52.2%, accounting for 10.1% of total revenue—the first time this ratio has reached double digits. GS Shop, the home shopping division, saw revenue of 253.2 billion Korean won and operating profit of 24.2 billion Korean won, up 2.3% and 108.6%, respectively. Sales of standalone beauty and fashion products performed well, with standalone product sales increasing 17%. GS Shop has improved its performance for four consecutive quarters since the fourth quarter of last year. The combined operating profit of supermarkets and home shopping reached 48.1 billion Korean won, exceeding 60% of GS25’s operating profit. While the second quarter saw operating profit growth across convenience stores, supermarkets, and home shopping, the third quarter was driven by supermarkets and home shopping compensating for the convenience store’s profit decline. A source from GS Retail stated, “We have achieved structural improvements by strengthening competitiveness across businesses such as convenience stores, supermarkets, and home shopping to broaden our profit structure. We will continue to focus on enhancing core business competitiveness and driving growth.”

content: GS Engineering & Construction reported a sharp year-on-year decline in third-quarter profitability on October 30, as lower building and housing revenue outweighed stronger plant activity. Revenue from the building and housing division fell 18.7 percent year on year to 1.4997 trillion Korean won, reflecting the downturn in the real estate market. Danwood, the company's Poland-based modular construction subsidiary, recorded 196.2 billion Korean won in orders. Through the first three quarters, GS E&C also secured construction rights worth 5.5 trillion Korean won in urban redevelopment projects and was selected as preferred bidder for the Mokdong Complex 12 reconstruction project and the Yeouido Eunha and Samik apartment projects. GS Engineering & Construction operates across building and housing, infrastructure and plant construction. Its portfolio includes residential developments, civil engineering projects, industrial facilities and modular construction activities. The combination gives the company exposure to both domestic housing demand and larger infrastructure and industrial contracts. For investors, the next key test is whether the company's recent presales and redevelopment wins translate into higher construction activity and revenue. At the same time, the plant division's contribution and the modular business provide additional areas to monitor as GS E&C manages a mixed housing and industrial cycle. He made the remarks while addressing a rally and discussion meeting organized on the occasion of the 48th founding anniversary of Jubo Dal at the Ojifa Khatun Primary School grounds in Subarnachar upazila, Noakhali, on Saturday afternoon. He noted that their relentless movement culminated in joining the 2024 mass uprising, which ultimately ousted the autocratic regime from the country. Zakaria, District Jubo Dal General Secretary Nurul Amin Khan, Executive Member Abul Kalam Azad, and Subarnachar Upazila Jubo Dal Member Secretary Nurul Huda, along with local leaders from various units. He’s a five-time Henry Ford Award winner, has covered the Olympic Games for TV5 and One Sports, called international volleyball for Volleyball World, and written and presented automotive stories for AutoIndustriya.com and Manila Bulletin. Before that, radio was a big part of his career. Nearly 25 years of it, as a presenter, program director and production lead. That range shows up in the way he works. Whether he’s writing, editing or speaking live on air, Eric has a knack for making technical or fast-moving subjects easier to understand without stripping away the detail that makes them interesting. Most luxury sedans don't look like they could hit 60 mph in 5.8 seconds, clear the quarter-mile in 14.5 seconds, and reach an electronically limited 149 mph on a track. Lexus recorded those figures with prototypes of the 300-hp V8 version of the second-generation Lexus GS. Not bad for a car dressed for a board meeting. Yet buyers often chase its Supra-related inline-six, which made 225 hp, or mistake it for the V6-powered ES 300. The engine with the bigger reputation might not be the better used-car buy. Under the GS 300's hood, six pistons rise and fall in one long row, with 24 valves controlling how the engine breathes. This 3.0-liter 2JZ-GE made 225 hp and 220 lb-ft in 1998, driving the rear wheels through an automatic. But the Supra family connection doesn't include the turbocharged Supra's hardware, and chasing that extra power means building a turbo car, not unlocking a factory secret. There's another trap under the Lexus badge. The ES 300's 1MZ-FE is a V6 mounted sideways for front-wheel drive. The GS 300 has a straight-six stretching lengthwise, with power going rearward. Open their hoods and the layout tells two different stories. Even service access changes; an ES repair complaint isn't evidence against the GS.In Japan, the second-generation Lexus GS was sold as the Toyota Aristo. The Aristo S300 used the same naturally aspirated 2JZ-GE as the U.S. GS 300, while the V300 packed a twin-turbo 2JZ-GTE rated at 280 PS (about 276 hp). The JZX100 Chaser Tourer V was a different car altogether, running a turbocharged 2.5-liter 1JZ-GTE. The 1998–2000 Lexus GS 400 hid serious speed behind familiar sheet metal. Its 4.0-liter 1UZ-FE V8 pumps out 300 hp and 310 lb-ft, an extra 75 hp and 90 lb-ft over the GS 300. Lexus's factory specifications put prototype 0–60 mph acceleration at 5.8 seconds, versus 7.6 for the six-cylinder. You get that speed without opening a turbo catalog. The four-cam V8 combines aluminum construction with variable valve timing to manage how its cylinders breathe. The GS 400 weighs just 55 pounds more than its six-cylinder sibling. A five-speed automatic feeds the rear wheels, while double-wishbone suspension guides them through bumps and corners. Steering-wheel E-shift buttons let you choose gears without reaching for the console. Traction control helps tame wheelspin. It's still an automatic, but Lexus gave the driver more to work with than a plain selector. The 2001 GS 430 trades 4.0 liters for 4.3 and brings 325 lb-ft at 3,400 rpm instead of the older V8's 310 at 4,000. Both make 300 hp; Lexus claimed the same 5.8-second run. If that car is better maintained, its extra torque makes it worth considering. A 300-hp Lexus V8 for $7,600? That's enough to make you check the listing twice. A 1998 GS 400 with 149,000 miles sold for that price on Bring a Trailer on June 22, 2026. Another '98, showing 48,000 miles, sold there for $12,000 on May 17. That's $4,400 extra for 101,000 fewer miles. Then inspect both. The cheaper car disclosed oil-pan and steering-rack leaks, plus a patch covering worn driver's-seat upholstery. The low-mileage one had a replacement instrument cluster calibrated to the removed unit's mileage and a faded dashboard beneath a pad. Neither was frozen in a showroom time capsule. Those winning bids also exclude buyer fees and taxes, and they aren't a market average or a guaranteed price range. Repairs can make a used Lexus bargain less charming. JDMBUYSELL reported a $15,950 Aristo median from 37 seller-reported sales dated August 2023 through October 2026, as of November 1, 2026. But those cars span generations and specifications. It's not proof of a fixed JDM premium over a GS 400. Compare cars, including fees and repairs. The GS 400 serves up luxury and muscle on the same plate: leather seats, walnut trim, dual-zone climate control, and a 300-hp V8. Before you fall for it, though, check dated receipts and mileage. Gates lists a timing-belt replacement interval of 90,000 miles or 72 months, whichever comes first. On this interference V8, a failed belt can mean pistons meeting valves, and nobody wants that introduction. Have a specialist review the belt-driven water pump, too. The S160's hydraulic brake booster, pump, accumulator, and ABS require model-specific pressure and electrical checks; warning lights or odd pump behavior deserve a repair estimate. Check stored faults, leaks, suspension wear, and the dashboard under any cover. Fading on one auction car doesn't make later-generation sticky-dashboard bulletins an S160 diagnosis. With proper maintenance and a clean inspection, this GS 400 makes a compelling used luxury sedan. But if repairs swallow the bargain, walk away. You came for a 300-hp Lexus, not a restoration project. Sources: Lexus, Toyota, Bring a Trailer, JDMBUYSELL, Gates We want to hear from you. title: Becky G’s Carolina Herrera Polka Dot Dress Goes Sheer at CFDA Awards - theFashionSpot
content: Home » Becky G’s Carolina Herrera Polka Dot Dress Goes Sheer at CFDA Awards Becky G brought a playful dose of retro glamour to the 2026 CFDA Fashion Awards in New York City. The singer stepped onto the red carpet in a polka-dot creation that mixed a vintage-inspired print with a more daring finish. Her look came straight from Carolina Herrera’s Spring/Summer 2027 collection. The sheer polka dot dress featured a strapless, figure-hugging silhouette in a powder blue shade covered in contrasting black dots. A sculpted sweetheart neckline framed her chest, while ruching throughout the bodice and skirt helped emphasize the fitted shape. The Carolina Herrera gown featured a striking contrast with a black sheer polka-dot panel that ran vertically down the center. This detail began with an oversized bow at the bust and cascaded down the front, creating a dramatic scarf-like effect against the blue fabric. The floor-length dress hugged Becky G’s curves before falling into a softly draped hem. A slit toward the front offered another glimpse of skin as she moved, while the lightweight fabric gave the gown plenty of movement. The original Carolina Herrera runway look featured the same mix of blue and black polka dots, along with the statement bow detail. Becky G kept her accessories understated enough to allow the patterned gown to command attention. She finished the ensemble with metallic silver strappy heels and delicate rings. Her dark hair was styled in voluminous curls that fell around her shoulders and down her back, adding to the old-school glamour of the outfit. Winged eyeliner, glowing skin, and a glossy nude lip rounded out her beauty look. The singer posed from every angle at the CFDA Fashion Awards, showing off both the fitted front and the strapless back of the Carolina Herrera design. With its sweetheart neckline, sheer accents, and bold mix of polka dots, the look offered a modern take on retro red carpet dressing. content: Jayendran GS is changing when mortgage lenders answer their most important question: whether a borrower qualifies. He built Prudent AI around a “Shift Left” model that moves income and eligibility decisions from the end of the mortgage process to the point of intake. Prudent AI’s Upfront Eligibility evaluates borrowers against each lender’s guidelines using verified data when a file is submitted. The technology now touches two out of every three non-QM loans in the United States, delivering eligibility answers 20 times faster and reducing the cost associated with files that cannot close by 95%. In January 2026, Jayendran expanded that model with Upfront Income, a universal income platform for agency and non-QM loans. It reviews income documents, performs quality and fraud checks and produces a qualifying income calculation within minutes. It expanded to rental income through a native integration with Fannie Mae’s Income Calculator. The results are significant. Angel Oak Mortgage Solutions increased loan volume by 200%, quadrupled underwriting productivity and improved pull-through from 22% to 65% without adding staff. American Heritage Lending reduced pre-approval time from three hours to 15 minutes and grew loan volume by 300%. Newfi Lending gives brokers qualifying income results in approximately seven minutes, reducing turn times from roughly 72 hours to as little as three. Across its client base, Prudent AI helps lenders move borrowers through their funnels three times faster at 2.5 times lower origination costs. title: Hyundai, Daewoo Lift Profits as GS, DL Slip in Q3 - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
■ Builders Report Mixed Third-Quarter Results
Samsung C&T's construction arm grows both revenue and operating profit
Hyundai and Daewoo post higher operating profit despite falling revenue
GS and DL see declines in both revenue and operating profit South Korea's largest builders extended their earnings recovery in the third quarter, improving profitability even as revenue declined. Low-margin projects launched when construction costs were surging have wound down, and cost-control efforts are paying off. Still, results diverged sharply across companies — hit by shrinking housing volumes and additional costs at overseas plant projects — and analysts say it is too early to call a full industry turnaround. Samsung C&T's (028260.KS) construction division posted revenue of 4.465 trillion won ($3.1 billion) and operating profit of 277 billion won, up 44.5% and 104.5% from a year earlier, according to filings with the Financial Supervisory Service's electronic disclosure system on the 2nd. Both top line and margins improved as high-tech work, including semiconductor plant construction, moved into full swing. Hyundai Engineering & Construction (000720.KS) saw revenue fall 20.3% to 6.2406 trillion won ($4.4 billion), but operating profit rose 114.2% to 221.7 billion won. Daewoo Engineering & Construction (047040.KS) reported revenue of 1.8424 trillion won ($1.3 billion), down 7.4%, while operating profit surged 223.7% to 183.2 billion won. Revenue slipped as the number of active sites fell, but cost management and a profitability-focused approach to project selection translated into stronger earnings, analysts said. GS E&C (006360.KS) and DL E&C (375500.KS), by contrast, continued to struggle. GS E&C posted revenue of 2.7442 trillion won ($1.9 billion) and operating profit of 95.5 billion won, down 14.5% and 35.7% respectively from a year earlier, weighed down by lower housing revenue. DL E&C reported revenue of 1.5065 trillion won ($1.1 billion) and operating profit of 107.3 billion won, down 21.0% and 8.1%. Schedule extensions and additional construction costs booked on the Shaheen project weighed on results. Industry officials say the completion of older low-margin sites and tighter cost controls are lifting profitability, but that this is hard to read as a broad recovery. A drop in new housing starts could leave a revenue gap ahead, and the burden of construction costs and financing expenses remains. Future earnings will hinge less on the sheer size of new orders than on the profitability of the work already secured and how quickly it converts into revenue. Whether improved operating profit feeds through to stronger cash flow and lower borrowings is also seen as a key gauge of builders' financial strength. title: GS E&C data breach exposes blind spots in Korea's smart apartments - The Korea Times
content: GS Engineering & Construction detected unauthorized external access to a system managing apartment community-facility reservations last Wednesday. The incident has raised concerns about the security of digital services used in Korea’s apartment complexes, where residents’ personal and access-related information is collected. The full extent of the exposure remains under investigation, and experts say similar systems used by other builders and public housing operators may also warrant review. When Park, a 56-year-old homemaker living in an apartment complex in Suwon, Gyeonggi Province, heard that GS Engineering & Construction (GS E&C) had recently detected unauthorized access to a system containing residents’ personal information, the news struck a nerve. “Sure, I’ve had my personal information exposed in the Coupang and SK Telecom data breaches, among many others. Over time, I found myself becoming less concerned. Everyone seemed to be getting hit, and it felt like I was just another number in a database,” she said. This time, however, it felt much closer to home, quite literally. “The information involved could reveal details about my own household. Our apartment complex, like many newer developments, relies on smart home services for everyday tasks. We use an app to track package deliveries and vehicle entry and exit, another to access the building, and I hear the sports center is introducing facial recognition for entry. If that kind of information gets exposed, it feels like someone might actually be able to track my every move.” Her concerns point to a growing vulnerability in a country where apartment living and digital technology are increasingly intertwined. Apartments account for a staggering 65.8 percent of all homes in Korea, according to 2025 data from the Ministry of Data and Statistics. As residential complexes adopt digital systems for everything from identity verification and building access to household device controls, they are also collecting more detailed information about residents and their routines. The security implications came into focus last Wednesday, when GS E&C said it had detected unauthorized external access to a system used to manage reservations for apartment community facilities. The potentially exposed data goes beyond basic identifying details, such as residents’ names, dates of birth and contact information. It also includes information about their residential status, whether they are the head of their household and radio-frequency identification (RFID) card numbers. Passwords were also listed among the affected information, although the company said they were encrypted. The full extent of the exposure remains under investigation. A panoramic view of apartment complexes in Seoul's Seongbuk District, Sunday / Yonhap Over the years, major construction companies have expanded their digital services for residents, offering platforms that combine smart home controls with building access, visitor registration and reservations for shared facilities. GS E&C operates its “Xi Home” platform, while Hyundai Engineering & Construction, Samsung C&T and Daewoo Engineering & Construction offer similar services across their apartment complexes. As these services have proliferated, however, information security may not have kept pace with the expansion, experts say, as construction has traditionally been viewed as a building-focused sector. The risks extend beyond the exposure of personal identifiers. RFID card numbers can be linked to systems controlling access to apartment buildings and shared facilities, while some complexes are starting to use facial recognition and other biometric data for entry. “RFID cards are used to control access to apartment buildings and shared facilities like saunas and gyms,” said Youm Heung-youl, an emeritus professor of information security at Soonchunhyang University. “The risks are even greater with facial recognition. Although there is no indication that biometric information was compromised in the GS E&C incident, its exposure could create further privacy risks, including the potential misuse of facial data in AI (artificial intelligence)-generated images.” The potential impact could also extend beyond a single apartment complex. “This is unlikely to be a problem limited to GS E&C. Other construction companies and public housing operators use similar systems. If multiple apartment complexes share a platform, a breach affecting one complex could spread to others. We need to examine whether these platforms are being managed securely,” he said. The professor called for a broader review of vulnerabilities in apartment management systems and their connections to external networks, noting that existing safeguards — including certified Internet of Things devices and separation between internal and shared networks — may not be sufficient.

Ex-FIFA GS Joins Historic Celebration as Africa Welcomes First Youth  Olympic Games Former FIFA Secretary General Fatma Samba Diouf Samoura joined the final procession of  Olympic Flame bearers in Dakar ahead of the official opening ceremony of the 2026 Youth Olympic Games, marking a significant moment in Senegal’s preparations to host the first Olympic event on African soil, BSNSports.com.ng reports. Samoura participated in the final leg of the relay alongside international personalities, including Senegalese social media star Khaby Lame, actor Omar Sy, wrestling champion Modou Lô and other prominent figures from  sports, entertainment and public life.شجع فريقك The final procession, held in a celebratory atmosphere in Dakar, brought together athletes, artists and residents to celebrate the Olympic spirit and the role of African youth in shaping the continent’s future. The Olympic Flame, which originated in Athens, travelled across Senegal for 47 days, covering more than 3,650 kilometres from Dakar to Ziguinchor and back to the capital. The nationwide relay passed through Thiès, Saint-Louis, Matam, Kaolack, Tambacounda, Kédougou and Kolda, among other locations, covering all 14 regions of the country. Approximately 450 torchbearers participated in more than 30 stages of the relay, which also featured sporting, cultural and educational activities designed to engage young people and local communities. The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games represent a historic breakthrough for Africa, as Senegal becomes the first African country to host an Olympic event. The Games mark a new chapter in the history of the Olympic movement, providing a global platform to showcase Africa’s sporting potential, cultural diversity and youthful population. Organisers expect approximately 2,700 athletes to compete across around 20 sporting disciplines, with the event being celebrated under the motto, "Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates." The hosting of the Games is also expected to strengthen Africa’s position in international sport while creating opportunities for young athletes to demonstrate their talents on a global stage. Samoura’s participation in the final torch relay reflects her longstanding contribution to international sports administration and development. A Senegalese national, she spent more than two decades working with the United Nations, holding senior positions in humanitarian affairs and development across several continents. In 2016, she made history when she was appointed FIFA Secretary General, becoming the first woman and the first African to occupy the position. She served in the role until 2023, overseeing the federation’s administration and contributing to the organisation of several FIFA World Cups. During her tenure, she also supported initiatives aimed at expanding football development, particularly women's football, while promoting improved governance and modernisation within the global football governing body. Following her departure from FIFA, Samoura has continued her involvement in international sports and development initiatives. She is currently a member of the FIA Senate and serves on the boards of organisations including Seed Project and African Collaborations Group (ACG). Her participation in the final Olympic Flame relay symbolised the connection between her experience in global sports administration and Africa’s growing ambitions on the international sporting stage. "To carry the flame is to carry a dream, and to pass it on is to pass on its energy," Samoura said. The final Olympic Flame relay preceded the opening ceremony of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, which took place on October 31 at the Abdoulaye Wade Stadium in Diamniadio. The ceremony was attended by Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye, International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry, Dakar 2026 Organising Committee President Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye and sports ministers representing African countries. The ceremony officially launched the first Youth Olympic Games to be staged on the African continent, placing Senegal at the centre of a historic moment for African sport. For Samoura and other prominent personalities who participated in the Flame relay, the occasion represented more than a ceremonial celebration.
